# Sample detection queries

Generated by running the shipped adapters over the synthetic demo fixtures in `packages/core/src/demo/fixtures.ts`. The input data is fictional and contains no customer telemetry, credentials or personal data.

> **None of these queries has been executed against a live SIEM.** The validation status on each block refers to structural checks performed inside this application only.

## Suspicious PowerShell Execution Followed by External Network Egress

**Objective.** Detect a PowerShell process launched with encoded, hidden or download-oriented arguments that is followed, on the same host and by the same account, by an outbound connection to a non-RFC1918 destination within a short window.

**Attack scenario.** After initial access through a malicious document or script, the adversary uses PowerShell to stage a loader with obfuscated arguments (encoded command, hidden window, download cradle). The loader then contacts an operator-controlled host to retrieve the next-stage implant or to register the beacon. Correlating the execution with the subsequent egress materially reduces the false-positive rate compared with alerting on PowerShell arguments alone.

**Telemetry.** microsoft / windows_sysmon, windows_security_events · **Correlation.** sequence, window 300s · **Severity.** high

**MITRE ATT&CK.** T1059.001 (Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell), T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols)

### Splunk Enterprise Security — SPL

Status: **Syntax Validated**

```text
``` Suspicious PowerShell Execution Followed by External Network Egress — powershell-exec-then-egress ```
``` Objective: Detect a PowerShell process launched with encoded, hidden or download-oriented arguments that is followed, on the same host and by the same account, by an outbound connection to a non-RFC1918 destination within a short window. ```
``` MITRE ATT&CK: T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell; T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols ```
index=sysmon sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational
| eval dfai_stage=case(
  (in(process_name, "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) AND (match(CommandLine, "(?i)(-enc(odedcommand)?|-e\\s|-w\\s*hidden|-windowstyle\\s*hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-ep\\s*bypass|downloadstring|downloadfile|invoke-webrequest|iwr\\s|frombase64string|iex\\s)")), "suspicious-powershell",
  (in(dest_port, 80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) AND (NOT match(dest_ip, "(?i)^(10\\.|127\\.|169\\.254\\.|192\\.168\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|100\\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\\.|::1$|fe80:|fc00:|fd)")), "external-egress",
  true(), null())
| where isnotnull(dfai_stage)
| stats count AS dfai_events, dc(dfai_stage) AS dfai_stage_count, values(dfai_stage) AS dfai_stages, min(_time) AS dfai_first_seen, max(_time) AS dfai_last_seen, min(eval(if(dfai_stage=="suspicious-powershell", _time, null()))) AS dfai_suspicious_powershell_time, min(eval(if(dfai_stage=="external-egress", _time, null()))) AS dfai_external_egress_time by host, user
| where dfai_stage_count==2
| eval dfai_window_seconds=dfai_last_seen-dfai_first_seen
| where dfai_window_seconds<=300
| where dfai_suspicious_powershell_time<=dfai_external_egress_time
| eval dfai_first_seen=strftime(dfai_first_seen, "%F %T"), dfai_last_seen=strftime(dfai_last_seen, "%F %T")
| eval dfai_severity="high", dfai_use_case="powershell-exec-then-egress"
```

### Microsoft Sentinel — KQL

Status: **Syntax Validated**

```text
// Suspicious PowerShell Execution Followed by External Network Egress — powershell-exec-then-egress
// Objective: Detect a PowerShell process launched with encoded, hidden or download-oriented arguments that is followed, on the same host and by the same account, by an outbound connection to a non-RFC1918 destination within a short window.
// MITRE ATT&CK: T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell; T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
let lookback = 86400s;
let correlationWindow = 300s;
// Stage 1 (suspicious-powershell): PowerShell launched with suspicious arguments
let dfai_suspicious_powershell = Event
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
    | where (Image in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) and (CommandLine matches regex "(-enc(odedcommand)?|-e\\s|-w\\s*hidden|-windowstyle\\s*hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-ep\\s*bypass|downloadstring|downloadfile|invoke-webrequest|iwr\\s|frombase64string|iex\\s)")
    | project dfai_suspicious_powershell_time = TimeGenerated, dfai_host_name = Computer, dfai_user_name = User, dfai_suspicious_powershell_count = 1;
// Stage 2 (external-egress): Outbound connection to an external destination
let dfai_external_egress = Event
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
    | where (DestinationPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) and (not (DestinationIp matches regex "^(10\\.|127\\.|169\\.254\\.|192\\.168\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|100\\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\\.|::1$|fe80:|fc00:|fd)"))
    | project dfai_external_egress_time = TimeGenerated, dfai_host_name = Computer, dfai_user_name = User, dfai_external_egress_count = 1;
dfai_suspicious_powershell
| join kind=inner (dfai_external_egress) on dfai_host_name, dfai_user_name
| where dfai_external_egress_time between (dfai_suspicious_powershell_time .. dfai_suspicious_powershell_time + correlationWindow)
| extend DetectionTime = dfai_external_egress_time, UseCaseId = "powershell-exec-then-egress", Severity = "high"
| project DetectionTime, dfai_host_name, dfai_user_name, dfai_suspicious_powershell_time, dfai_external_egress_time, UseCaseId, Severity
```

**Mapping required**

- `process.name` — Requires a QRadar custom event property (regex/JSON extraction) to exist on the log source before this reference resolves.
- `process.command_line` — Command line is not a normalised AQL column. Requires a QRadar custom event property (regex/JSON extraction) to exist on the log source before this reference resolves.
- `process.parent.name` — Requires a QRadar custom event property (regex/JSON extraction) to exist on the log source before this reference resolves.
- `host.name` — AQL exposes the log source rather than a normalised hostname: use `LOGSOURCENAME(logsourceid)` or a custom property.

**Platform configuration required**

- AQL has no sequence operator. Build one building block per stage, then a rule with "when these building blocks occur in sequence within 5 minutes" and the counting property set to host.name, user.name.
- Use Rule Response > Dispatch New Event with an appropriate severity/credibility/relevance so the offense is raised with the intended magnitude.
- Any referenced property that is not a standard normalised column requires a Custom Event Property (regex or JSON) created on the relevant log source, optimised for search, before the query will return data.
- Confirm exact log source type strings in Admin > Log Sources; DSM naming differs between QRadar versions.

### Elastic Security — EQL / ES|QL

Status: **Syntax Validated**

```text
// Suspicious PowerShell Execution Followed by External Network Egress — powershell-exec-then-egress
// Objective: Detect a PowerShell process launched with encoded, hidden or download-oriented arguments that is followed, on the same host and by the same account, by an outbound connection to a non-RFC1918 destination within a short window.
// MITRE ATT&CK: T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell; T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
// Index pattern(s): logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*

// ===== EQL (Elastic Query Language) =====
sequence by host.name, user.name with maxspan=5m
  [ any where (process.name in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) and (process.command_line regex~ "(-enc(odedcommand)?|-e\\s|-w\\s*hidden|-windowstyle\\s*hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-ep\\s*bypass|downloadstring|downloadfile|invoke-webrequest|iwr\\s|frombase64string|iex\\s)") ]
  [ any where (destination.port in (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) and (not destination.ip regex~ "^(10\\.|127\\.|169\\.254\\.|192\\.168\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|100\\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\\.|::1$|fe80:|fc00:|fd)") ]
// ===== ES|QL =====
FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*
| WHERE ((process.name IN ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) AND (process.command_line RLIKE "(-enc(odedcommand)?|-e\\s|-w\\s*hidden|-windowstyle\\s*hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-ep\\s*bypass|downloadstring|downloadfile|invoke-webrequest|iwr\\s|frombase64string|iex\\s)")) OR ((destination.port IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) AND (NOT destination.ip RLIKE "^(10\\.|127\\.|169\\.254\\.|192\\.168\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|100\\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\\.|::1$|fe80:|fc00:|fd)"))
| EVAL dfai_stage = CASE((process.name IN ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) AND (process.command_line RLIKE "(-enc(odedcommand)?|-e\\s|-w\\s*hidden|-windowstyle\\s*hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-ep\\s*bypass|downloadstring|downloadfile|invoke-webrequest|iwr\\s|frombase64string|iex\\s)"), "suspicious-powershell", (destination.port IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) AND (NOT destination.ip RLIKE "^(10\\.|127\\.|169\\.254\\.|192\\.168\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|100\\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\\.|::1$|fe80:|fc00:|fd)"), "external-egress", NULL)
| WHERE dfai_stage IS NOT NULL
| STATS dfai_events = COUNT(*), dfai_first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), dfai_last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), dfai_stage_count = COUNT_DISTINCT(dfai_stage) BY host.name, user.name
| WHERE dfai_stage_count == 2
| SORT dfai_events DESC
| LIMIT 100
```

### Securonix — Spotter Query Language

Status: **Mapping Required**

```text
// Suspicious PowerShell Execution Followed by External Network Egress — powershell-exec-then-egress
// Objective: Detect a PowerShell process launched with encoded, hidden or download-oriented arguments that is followed, on the same host and by the same account, by an outbound connection to a non-RFC1918 destination within a short window.
// Spotter searches below are for hunting and policy validation.
// The production detection is a Securonix policy (see configuration guidance).

// Stage 1 (suspicious-powershell): PowerShell launched with suspicious arguments
index = activity AND rg_functionality = "Endpoint Management Systems" AND (destinationprocessname IN ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) AND (<<MAPPING_REQUIRED:process.command_line>> CONTAINS "<<REGEX_UNSUPPORTED>>")

// Stage 2 (external-egress): Outbound connection to an external destination
index = activity AND rg_functionality = "Endpoint Management Systems" AND (destinationport IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) AND (NOT destinationaddress CONTAINS "<<REGEX_UNSUPPORTED>>")
```

**Mapping required**

- `process.command_line` — Securonix normalisation is import-connector dependent; confirm the policy field in Spotter before promoting the query.

**Platform configuration required**

- Create one policy per stage, then chain them with a Violation Chain / Threat Model so that stage order is enforced within 5m, correlated on host.name, user.name.
- Risk scoring, peer-group baselines, whitelists and the threat-model association are console-side configuration and cannot be represented in Spotter query text.
- Confirm every attribute name against your import connector normalisation: Securonix field availability is deployment specific.

### FortiSIEM — Event Search / Rule Expression

Status: **Not Validated**

```text
# Suspicious PowerShell Execution Followed by External Network Egress — powershell-exec-then-egress
# Objective: Detect a PowerShell process launched with encoded, hidden or download-oriented arguments that is followed, on the same host and by the same account, by an outbound connection to a non-RFC1918 destination within a short window.
# Expressions below are FortiSIEM Analytics event-search filters, one per
# rule sub-pattern. The rule itself is defined in Resources > Rules.

# SubPattern 1 (suspicious-powershell): PowerShell launched with suspicious arguments
eventType CONTAIN "Win-Sysmon" AND (procName IN ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell_ise.exe")) AND (command REGEXP "(-enc(odedcommand)?|-e\\s|-w\\s*hidden|-windowstyle\\s*hidden|-nop|-noprofile|-ep\\s*bypass|downloadstring|downloadfile|invoke-webrequest|iwr\\s|frombase64string|iex\\s)")

# SubPattern 2 (external-egress): Outbound connection to an external destination
eventType CONTAIN "Win-Sysmon" AND (destIpPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53, 4444, 8888)) AND (NOT destIpAddr REGEXP "^(10\\.|127\\.|169\\.254\\.|192\\.168\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|100\\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-7])\\.|::1$|fe80:|fc00:|fd)")

# Rule outline (configure in Resources > Rules):
#   Severity: high
#   Evaluation window: 5m
#   SubPattern 1 "suspicious-powershell": filter above, GROUP BY host.name, user.name, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1
#   SubPattern 2 "external-egress": filter above, GROUP BY host.name, user.name, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1
#   Pattern relationship: FOLLOWED_BY (ordered) across sub-patterns, within 5m
```

**Platform configuration required**

- Build the rule with one sub-pattern per stage. Set the group-by attributes to host.name, user.name and the pattern time window to 5m.
- Incident title, category, notification policy and remediation action are rule properties configured in the GUI, not part of the search expression.
- Verify every attribute exists for the device type in Analytics > Event Attributes; FortiSIEM attribute coverage is parser dependent.

## Repeated Authentication Failures Followed by Successful Sign-in

**Objective.** Detect an account that accumulates a burst of failed authentications and then authenticates successfully from the same source address within the same window, indicating a likely successful password-guessing or spray attempt.

**Attack scenario.** An adversary with a list of valid usernames attempts a small number of common passwords against many accounts, or many passwords against one account. When a guess succeeds the failure burst is immediately followed by a successful logon from the same source. Alerting on the failure burst alone is noisy; pairing it with the success provides high-confidence evidence of account compromise.

**Telemetry.** microsoft / windows_security_events · **Correlation.** sequence, window 900s, threshold 10 · **Severity.** high

**MITRE ATT&CK.** T1110.003 (Brute Force: Password Spraying), T1078 (Valid Accounts)

| Platform | Validation status | Mapping gaps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Splunk Enterprise Security | Syntax Validated | none |
| Microsoft Sentinel | Syntax Validated | none |

| Elastic Security | Syntax Validated | none |

| FortiSIEM | Mapping Required | `logon.type` |
| Sigma | Syntax Validated | none |

### Splunk Enterprise Security — SPL

Status: **Syntax Validated**

```text
``` Repeated Authentication Failures Followed by Successful Sign-in — password-spray-then-success ```

| eval dfai_stage=case(
```

### Microsoft Sentinel — KQL

Status: **Syntax Validated**

```text
// Repeated Authentication Failures Followed by Successful Sign-in — password-spray-then-success
// Objective: Detect an account that accumulates a burst of failed authentications and then authenticates successfully from the same source address within the same window, indicating a likely successful password-guessing or spray attempt.
// MITRE ATT&CK: T1110.003 Brute Force: Password Spraying; T1078 Valid Accounts
let lookback = 86400s;
let correlationWindow = 900s;
// Stage 1 (failed-logons): Burst of failed logons
let dfai_failed_logons = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
    | where (EventID == 4625) and (LogonType in (3, 8, 10)) and (TargetUserName !contains "$")
    | project dfai_failed_logons_time = TimeGenerated, dfai_user_name = TargetUserName, dfai_source_ip = IpAddress, dfai_failed_logons_count = 1;
// Stage 2 (successful-logon): Successful logon from the same source
let dfai_successful_logon = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
    | where (EventID == 4624) and (LogonType in (3, 8, 10))
    | project dfai_successful_logon_time = TimeGenerated, dfai_user_name = TargetUserName, dfai_source_ip = IpAddress, dfai_successful_logon_count = 1;
dfai_failed_logons
| join kind=inner (dfai_successful_logon) on dfai_user_name, dfai_source_ip
| where dfai_successful_logon_time between (dfai_failed_logons_time .. dfai_failed_logons_time + correlationWindow)
| extend DetectionTime = dfai_successful_logon_time, UseCaseId = "password-spray-then-success", Severity = "high"
| project DetectionTime, dfai_user_name, dfai_source_ip, dfai_failed_logons_time, dfai_successful_logon_time, UseCaseId, Severity
```

```text
LAST 15 MINUTES

-- Stage 2 (successful-logon): Successful logon from the same source
SELECT QIDNAME(qid) AS event_name, DATEFORMAT(starttime, 'YYYY-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') AS event_time, username, sourceip
FROM events
WHERE logsourcetype = 'Microsoft Windows Security Event Log' AND (<<MAPPING_REQUIRED:event.code>> = 4624) AND (<<MAPPING_REQUIRED:logon.type>> IN (3, 8, 10))
LAST 15 MINUTES
```

**Mapping required**

- `event.code` — Use the QRadar QID or category rather than a raw event id: `qid` / `category` are the supported discriminators in AQL.
- `logon.type` — Requires a QRadar custom event property (regex/JSON extraction) to exist on the log source before this reference resolves.
- `host.name` — AQL exposes the log source rather than a normalised hostname: use `LOGSOURCENAME(logsourceid)` or a custom property.

**Platform configuration required**

- AQL has no sequence operator. Build one building block per stage, then a rule with "when these building blocks occur in sequence within 15 minutes" and the counting property set to user.name, source.ip.
- Use Rule Response > Dispatch New Event with an appropriate severity/credibility/relevance so the offense is raised with the intended magnitude.
- Any referenced property that is not a standard normalised column requires a Custom Event Property (regex or JSON) created on the relevant log source, optimised for search, before the query will return data.
- Confirm exact log source type strings in Admin > Log Sources; DSM naming differs between QRadar versions.

### Elastic Security — EQL / ES|QL

Status: **Syntax Validated**

```text
// Repeated Authentication Failures Followed by Successful Sign-in — password-spray-then-success
// Objective: Detect an account that accumulates a burst of failed authentications and then authenticates successfully from the same source address within the same window, indicating a likely successful password-guessing or spray attempt.
// MITRE ATT&CK: T1110.003 Brute Force: Password Spraying; T1078 Valid Accounts
// Index pattern(s): logs-windows.*,winlogbeat-*

// ===== EQL (Elastic Query Language) =====
sequence by user.name, source.ip with maxspan=15m
  [ any where (winlog.event_id == 4625) and (winlog.event_data.LogonType in (3, 8, 10)) and (not user.name like~ "*$*") ]
  [ any where (winlog.event_id == 4624) and (winlog.event_data.LogonType in (3, 8, 10)) ]
// ===== ES|QL =====
FROM logs-windows.*,winlogbeat-*
| WHERE ((winlog.event_id == 4625) AND (winlog.event_data.LogonType IN (3, 8, 10)) AND (NOT user.name LIKE "*$*")) OR ((winlog.event_id == 4624) AND (winlog.event_data.LogonType IN (3, 8, 10)))
| EVAL dfai_stage = CASE((winlog.event_id == 4625) AND (winlog.event_data.LogonType IN (3, 8, 10)) AND (NOT user.name LIKE "*$*"), "failed-logons", (winlog.event_id == 4624) AND (winlog.event_data.LogonType IN (3, 8, 10)), "successful-logon", NULL)
| WHERE dfai_stage IS NOT NULL
| STATS dfai_events = COUNT(*), dfai_first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), dfai_last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), dfai_stage_count = COUNT_DISTINCT(dfai_stage) BY user.name, source.ip
| WHERE dfai_stage_count == 2 AND dfai_events >= 10
| SORT dfai_events DESC
| LIMIT 100
```

### FortiSIEM — Event Search / Rule Expression

Status: **Mapping Required**

```text
# Repeated Authentication Failures Followed by Successful Sign-in — password-spray-then-success
# Objective: Detect an account that accumulates a burst of failed authentications and then authenticates successfully from the same source address within the same window, indicating a likely successful password-guessing or spray attempt.
# Expressions below are FortiSIEM Analytics event-search filters, one per
# rule sub-pattern. The rule itself is defined in Resources > Rules.

# SubPattern 1 (failed-logons): Burst of failed logons
eventType CONTAIN "Win-Security" AND (eventType = 4625) AND (<<MAPPING_REQUIRED:logon.type>> IN (3, 8, 10)) AND (user NOT CONTAIN "$")

# SubPattern 2 (successful-logon): Successful logon from the same source
eventType CONTAIN "Win-Security" AND (eventType = 4624) AND (<<MAPPING_REQUIRED:logon.type>> IN (3, 8, 10))

# Rule outline (configure in Resources > Rules):
#   Severity: high
#   Evaluation window: 15m
#   SubPattern 1 "failed-logons": filter above, GROUP BY user.name, source.ip, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1
#   SubPattern 2 "successful-logon": filter above, GROUP BY user.name, source.ip, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1
#   Pattern relationship: FOLLOWED_BY (ordered) across sub-patterns, within 15m
```

**Mapping required**

- `logon.type` — FortiSIEM event attribute availability depends on the active parser for the device type; confirm the attribute name in Analytics > Event Attributes.

**Platform configuration required**

- Build the rule with one sub-pattern per stage. Set the group-by attributes to user.name, source.ip and the pattern time window to 15m.
- Incident title, category, notification policy and remediation action are rule properties configured in the GUI, not part of the search expression.
- Verify every attribute exists for the device type in Analytics > Event Attributes; FortiSIEM attribute coverage is parser dependent.
